items.rationale: Correct shifted-binomial PMF, including support and zero elsewhere; all tabulated probabilities agree. Expectation 59/3 and variance 10/9 are correct and justified.
Correctly identifies the conditioning event as N ≤ 1 and computes the conditional expectation as 80/(32+80) = 5/7.
Correctly conditions on the fourth light being red and the fifth green. Independence preserves the first three indicators' joint distribution, giving conditional variance 3(1/3)(2/3) = 2/3.
Correctly justifies equal likelihood of the three-red-light configurations and counts favorable configurations, obtaining C(3,2)C(2,1)/C(5,3) = 3/5.
Correct PMF: probability 1/4 at each of 20, 21, 22, and 23 minutes, and zero elsewhere.
Correctly partitions the conditioning event into the two exclusive sole-arrival possibilities and uses independence. The resulting conditional probability 163/403 is correct.
Correctly conditions on all four equally likely waiting times, using N ≤ 2+X. The cumulative probabilities and their average 909/972 = 101/108 are correct.
Correctly establishes that X = 3 guarantees S ≤ J, so the joint-event numerator is 1/4. Dividing by 101/108 yields the correct conditional probability 27/101.
Correctly declares the statement true and proves P(A intersect B-complement) = P(A)P(B-complement) by partitioning A and using independence. The proof also covers events of probability zero or one.

Valid counterexample on six equally likely outcomes. P(C) = 2/3 satisfies the hypothesis; given C, the joint probability 1/4 equals the product of marginals. Given its complement, the joint probability is 1/2 while the product is 1/4, disproving the conclusion.

Correctly proves variance additivity using independence and then the inequality using nonnegativity of variance. The finite-variance qualification matches the usual setting implicit in the official solution. The additional equality characterization is also correct in that setting.
